question: The Constitution of India is a sovereign socialist secular democratic republic with a ______________ system of government.
solution_text:
The correct answer is parliamentary.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Preamble of the Constitution of India declares India to be a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic with a parliamentary system of government. (संसदीय शासन प्रणाली — भारत)

 

• In a parliamentary system, the executive is drawn from and is collectively responsible to the legislature (Parliament); the President is the nominal/constitutional head, while the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers wield real executive power.

 

• India adopted this British-style Westminster model because of the close executive-legislature relationship, the principle of collective responsibility, and the familiarity Indian leaders had with the system from the colonial period.

 

• The words "socialist" and "secular" were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India follows a federal structure with a unitary bias — power is divided between the Union and the States (Seventh Schedule), but the Centre retains overriding authority in several respects.

 

• The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950; it is the longest written constitution of any sovereign country.

 

NOTE

 

• Unitary (Option 1): Describes a system where all power is concentrated at the centre, unlike India's federal set-up.

 

• Monarchical (Option 3): Refers to rule by a hereditary king/queen; India has no monarch and abolished privy purses/princely rule.

 

• Presidential (Option 4): As in the USA, the executive is independent of and not responsible to the legislature; India's President is head of state, not head of government.

question: Ahmadnagar was finally annexed by the Mughals in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1632.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ahmadnagar Sultanate, founded in 1490 by Ahmad Nizam Shah, was one of the five Deccan Sultanates and was gradually absorbed into the Mughal Empire during the reign of emperor Shah Jahan. (अहमदनगर सल्तनत — मुग़ल साम्राज्य में विलय)

 

• Mughal pressure on Ahmadnagar had begun as early as Akbar's reign (Mughal forces had captured Ahmadnagar city itself in 1600), but the kingdom kept resisting for decades under able regents such as Malik Ambar, who used guerrilla tactics against Mughal expansion.

 

• Sustained Mughal campaigns in the early 1630s under Shah Jahan finally broke this resistance, and general-knowledge compilations for competitive exams list 1632 as the year of the final annexation of Ahmadnagar by the Mughals.

 

• This annexation effectively ended the independent rule of the Nizam Shahi dynasty, with most of its territory absorbed into the Mughal Empire and the remainder later going to the Sultanate of Bijapur.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Resistance in the region continued even after this, notably under Shahji Bhonsle (father of Chhatrapati Shivaji), who kept fighting on behalf of the Nizam Shahi cause for some years.

 

• The fort of Daulatabad, the symbolic capital of the Deccan sultans, was a key strategic target of these Mughal campaigns.

 

NOTE

 

• 1627 (Option 1): This is close to the year Emperor Jahangir died (1627) and Shah Jahan's accession followed, but it does not mark Ahmadnagar's annexation.

 

• 1630 (Option 3): Mughal campaigns against Ahmadnagar were intensifying around this time under Shah Jahan, but the sultanate's resistance had not yet been finally broken.

 

• 1635 (Option 4): Mughal consolidation in the Deccan continued into the mid-1630s, but this is not the year given for the final annexation.

question: Which of the following major Indian crops requires high temperature (above 25°C) and high humidity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rice.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rice is a kharif crop that requires high temperature (above 25°C) and high humidity, together with abundant water, making it the staple crop of India's high-rainfall regions. (चावल — उच्च तापमान और आर्द्रता वाली फसल)

 

• It is grown extensively in states such as West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu, sown with the onset of the South-West Monsoon (June-July) and harvested around September-October.

 

• Rice cultivation typically needs standing water in the field for most of its growth period, which is why it thrives best in humid, high-temperature, high-rainfall tracts and river deltas.

 

• India is among the world's largest producers and exporters of rice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Wheat, a rabi crop, needs a cool climate during growth and a relatively warm, dry spell at ripening — conditions opposite to those needed for rice.

 

• Gram and Peas are rabi pulses, requiring cool, comparatively dry winter conditions rather than high temperature and humidity.

 

NOTE

 

• Gram (Option 1) and Peas (Option 2): Rabi pulses grown in the cool, dry winter season, unlike rice.

 

• Wheat (Option 4): A rabi crop requiring cool temperatures for growth and moderate rainfall, not high heat and humidity.

question: ______ - time graph shows speed of an object.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Distance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A distance-time graph plots the distance covered by a moving object against time; the slope (gradient) of this graph at any instant gives the object's speed. (दूरी-समय ग्राफ — चाल)

 

• A steeper slope means a higher speed, a horizontal (flat) line means the object is at rest, and a straight line of constant slope represents uniform speed.

 

• This is different from a velocity-time graph, whose slope gives acceleration and whose area under the curve gives displacement.

 

• Speed is a scalar quantity (only magnitude), which is why it is derived from distance — itself a scalar — rather than from displacement or velocity, which are vector quantities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• On a velocity-time graph: area under the curve = displacement, and slope = acceleration.

 

• On a displacement-time graph: the slope gives velocity, a vector, rather than plain scalar speed.

 

NOTE

 

• Velocity (Option 1): The slope of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration, not speed.

 

• Displacement (Option 3): The slope of a displacement-time graph gives velocity, a vector quantity distinct from scalar speed.

 

• Acceleration (Option 4): An acceleration-time graph shows how acceleration varies with time and does not directly give speed.

question: Which nutrient is chlorella rich in?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Protein.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chlorella is a genus of single-celled green freshwater algae that is exceptionally rich in protein, containing up to 50-60% protein by dry weight, along with vitamins, minerals, and chlorophyll. (क्लोरेला शैवाल — प्रोटीन का समृद्ध स्रोत)

 

• Because of its high protein content and near-complete amino acid profile, Chlorella is widely marketed as a dietary supplement and is being explored as a sustainable, alternative source of protein.

 

• It also contains substantial chlorophyll, which is why Chlorella supplements are often promoted for their nutrient-dense and detoxifying properties.

 

• Chlorella was among the earliest algae studied for potential use as a compact, high-yield food source, including in famine-relief and space-travel research.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Spirulina, another blue-green algae, is similarly known for its very high protein content and is a popular dietary supplement alongside Chlorella.

 

NOTE

 

• Roughage (Option 1): Refers to dietary fibre, mainly obtained from whole grains, fruits and vegetables — not Chlorella's defining nutrient.

 

• Carbohydrates (Option 2): Present in Chlorella but in much smaller proportion than protein.

 

• Fats (Option 3): Present only in small amounts; not the nutrient Chlorella is best known for.

question: Who has become the first woman director general of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nallathamby Kalaiselvi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Nallathamby Kalaiselvi became the first woman Director General of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) in August 2022, also taking charge as Secretary, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR). (सीएसआईआर की पहली महिला महानिदेशक — नल्लाथम्बी कलईसेल्वी)

 

• She is an eminent electrochemical scientist recognised for her work on lithium-ion and sodium-ion battery materials, and previously served as Director of CSIR-Central Electrochemical Research Institute (CECRI), Karaikudi.

 

• CSIR, established in 1942, is India's premier autonomous R&D organisation under the Ministry of Science and Technology, with the Prime Minister of India as its ex-officio President.

 

• Her appointment was widely noted as a landmark moment for women's leadership in Indian scientific administration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• CSIR runs a nationwide network of national laboratories spanning fields such as aerospace, biotechnology, chemicals, mining, and food science.

 

NOTE

 

• Sanjay Verma, Vinod Aggarwal, Prakash Chand (Options 1, 2 and 4): These names are not associated with the position of CSIR Director General; they serve as distractor options.

question: McMahon line is a line which separates china and which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arunachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The McMahon Line is the boundary agreed upon between British India and Tibet at the Simla Convention of 1914, running along the crest of the Eastern Himalayas and separating Tibet (China) from India's north-eastern state of Arunachal Pradesh. (मैकमोहन रेखा — अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

 

• It is named after Sir Henry McMahon, the British administrator who negotiated the boundary on behalf of British India.

 

• China does not recognise the McMahon Line as the official international boundary, and this remains central to the ongoing India-China border dispute in the eastern sector, which China refers to as "South Tibet."

 

• The line runs for roughly 890 km, from the tri-junction with Bhutan to the tri-junction with Myanmar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other disputed India-China border stretches include the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in the Ladakh (Aksai Chin) sector, in the western Himalayas.

 

NOTE

 

• Sikkim (Option 1): Borders China/Tibet, but its boundary is defined separately, not by the McMahon Line.

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 2): Shares a border with China in the middle Himalayan sector, unrelated to the McMahon Line.

 

• Jammu and Kashmir (Option 4): Its border dispute with China concerns Aksai Chin in the western sector, not the McMahon Line.

question: The Paris Indian Society was an Indian nationalist organisation founded in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1905.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Paris Indian Society was an Indian nationalist organisation founded in Paris in 1905, under the patronage of Madame Bhikaji Cama, Munchershah Burjorji Godrej, and S. R. Rana. (पेरिस इंडियन सोसाइटी — 1905)

 

• It functioned in association with the Indian Home Rule Society, established around the same period in London by Shyamji Krishna Varma, aimed at promoting Indian self-rule among Indians living in Europe.

 

• Paris became an important base for Indian revolutionary nationalists in Europe, particularly as British pressure made open political activity in London increasingly difficult.

 

• Madame Cama went on to become a leading figure of the revolutionary movement abroad, famously unfurling an early version of the Indian flag in Stuttgart, Germany, in 1907.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India House in London, founded in 1905 by Shyamji Krishna Varma, was another key overseas centre of Indian nationalist and revolutionary activity in this period.

 

NOTE

 

• 1907 (Option 1), 1909 (Option 3), 1900 (Option 4): These years are close to other events of the overseas revolutionary movement (such as Madame Cama's 1907 flag unfurling), but none of them marks the founding of the Paris Indian Society.

question: Droupadi Murmu was elected the _______ President of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Droupadi Murmu was elected as the 15th President of India, taking oath of office on 25 July 2022, succeeding Ram Nath Kovind. (द्रौपदी मुर्मू — भारत की 15वीं राष्ट्रपति)

 

• She is the first person from a tribal (Santhal) community to hold the office of President of India, and only the second woman President, after Pratibha Patil.

 

• Before becoming President, she served as Governor of Jharkhand (2015-2021) — the first woman to hold that post — and earlier held ministerial and legislative positions in Odisha.

 

• She contested the 2022 presidential election as the candidate of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), defeating opposition candidate Yashwant Sinha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's President is elected by an Electoral College comprising elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of State/UT Legislative Assemblies.

 

NOTE

 

• 16th, 17th, 18th (Options 4, 2 and 1): Incorrect ordinal positions; Droupadi Murmu is officially reckoned as India's 15th President.

question: What is the commercial unit of electric energy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kilowatt hour.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The commercial unit of electric energy is the kilowatt-hour (kWh), commonly known as a "unit" of electricity on household bills. (विद्युत ऊर्जा की व्यावसायिक इकाई — किलोवाट घंटा)

 

• 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ joules, i.e., the energy consumed by a device rated at 1 kilowatt operating continuously for 1 hour.

 

• The SI unit of energy is the joule, but since a joule is far too small for everyday electricity billing, the much larger kilowatt-hour is used for commercial/practical purposes.

 

• Household and commercial electricity meters record consumption in kWh, which utility companies use to calculate bills.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Watt is the SI unit of power (the rate of energy transfer), not energy itself; 1 Watt = 1 Joule/second.

 

NOTE

 

• Watt-hour (Option 1): A valid, smaller unit of energy (1/1000th of a kWh), but not the standard unit used for commercial billing.

 

• Watt per hour (Option 2) and Kilowatt per hour (Option 4): Neither is a valid unit of energy — "per hour" incorrectly implies a rate of change rather than an accumulated quantity of energy.

question: In early 1610, who discovered with his newly invented telescope that Jupiter has four moons?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Galileo Galilei.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In January 1610, Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei, using his self-improved telescope, discovered the four largest moons of Jupiter — Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto — now collectively called the Galilean moons. (गैलीलियो गैलिली — बृहस्पति के चार चंद्रमा)

 

• This discovery was highly significant because it showed that not every celestial body orbits the Earth, providing strong observational support for the heliocentric (Sun-centred) model proposed by Copernicus.

 

• Galileo published his findings in the treatise *Sidereus Nuncius* ("Starry Messenger") in 1610.

 

• He is also credited with improving telescope design and making pioneering observations of the Moon's surface, sunspots, and the phases of Venus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Simon Marius, a contemporary German astronomer, independently observed Jupiter's moons around the same time and gave them their modern names (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto).

 

NOTE

 

• Simon Marius (Option 1): Made independent observations of the moons around the same period and later named them, but Galileo is credited with the discovery and publication priority.

 

• Tycho Brahe (Option 2): A pre-telescopic Danish astronomer famed for precise naked-eye observations; he died in 1601, before this discovery was made.

 

• Johannes Kepler (Option 4): Renowned for his laws of planetary motion; he supported and publicised Galileo's findings but did not make this particular discovery.

question: By which name is the birthday of Lord Krishna famous?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Janmashtami.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The birthday of Lord Krishna is celebrated as Janmashtami (also called Krishna Janmashtami or Gokulashtami), observed on the Ashtami (eighth day) of the Krishna Paksha (dark fortnight) in the month of Bhadrapada. (जन्माष्टमी — भगवान कृष्ण का जन्मदिन)

 

• The festival is marked by fasting, devotional singing (bhajans/kirtans), midnight worship — since Krishna is believed to have been born at midnight — and re-enactments of scenes from his life (Raslila).

 

• In many regions, especially Maharashtra, the festival features the Dahi Handi tradition, where young men form human pyramids to break a pot of curd/butter hung high above.

 

• It is one of the most widely and enthusiastically celebrated festivals across India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mahashtami and Mahanavmi are the eighth and ninth days of Navratri, associated with the worship of Goddess Durga, not Krishna.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahashtami (Option 1) and Mahanavmi (Option 2): Days within the Navratri festival dedicated to Goddess Durga, unrelated to Krishna's birth.

 

• Akshaya Tritiya (Option 4): An auspicious day in the Hindu calendar associated with new beginnings and prosperity, not connected to Krishna's birthday.

question: Which of the following is NOT a goal for the Green Revolution?
option_3: Rise in production of food grains
solution_text:
The correct answer is Use of fertilisers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution in India (from the mid-1960s, associated with scientists such as M. S. Swaminathan and Norman Borlaug's High Yielding Variety seeds) was aimed at specific outcome-based goals: raising crop productivity, boosting food-grain production, and expanding irrigated area to achieve national food self-sufficiency. (हरित क्रांति — लक्ष्य बनाम साधन)

 

• Use of fertilisers was one of the important means/inputs adopted to achieve these goals — alongside High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, assured irrigation and pesticides — rather than being itself an end goal of the Green Revolution.

 

• The actual stated goals concerned outcomes: higher productivity per hectare, greater overall food-grain production, and expansion of irrigation infrastructure to support intensive, HYV-based farming.

 

• The Green Revolution transformed India from a food-deficit nation dependent on imports (such as PL-480 wheat from the USA) into a food-surplus nation by the late 1970s.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution was concentrated mainly in Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh, and was largely restricted to wheat and rice.

 

• Common criticisms of the Green Revolution include regional disparities, groundwater depletion, and soil degradation from excessive fertiliser/pesticide use.

 

NOTE

 

• Rise in crop productivity (Option 1): A genuine stated goal — raising output per unit area of land.

 

• Rise in production of food grains (Option 3): A genuine stated goal — achieving national food self-sufficiency.

 

• Expansion of irrigation (Option 4): A genuine stated goal — bringing more area under assured irrigation to support HYV cultivation.

question: Which of the following metals was used to make weapons and tools in Harappan cities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Copper.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Harappan (Indus Valley) Civilisation belonged to the Bronze Age, and its people primarily used copper (and its alloy bronze, made by mixing copper with tin) to make weapons, tools, vessels and ornaments. (हड़प्पा सभ्यता — तांबे का प्रयोग)

 

• Harappans obtained copper ore mainly from the Khetri mines of Rajasthan, as well as from sources in present-day Oman and Baluchistan.

 

• Iron was not known to the Harappans — it came into common use in India only in the later Vedic/Iron Age, well after the decline of the Indus Valley Civilisation.

 

• Harappan metallurgy also included gold and silver for ornaments, but everyday tools and weapons (axes, chisels, knives, fish-hooks) were predominantly made of copper/bronze.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Harappans were also skilled in bead-making, seal-carving, and the use of standardised weights and measures, alongside their metallurgical expertise.

 

NOTE

 

• Silver (Option 1) and Gold (Option 2): Used mainly for ornaments and jewellery, not for weapons or everyday tools.

 

• Iron (Option 4): Unknown to the Harappans; it became prevalent in India only in the subsequent Iron Age.

question: The executive power of the Union is vested in the:
option_1: Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister
option_3: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
solution_text:
The correct answer is President.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Article 53 of the Constitution of India, the executive power of the Union is vested in the President, to be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him, in accordance with the Constitution. (अनुच्छेद 53 — राष्ट्रपति में निहित कार्यपालिका शक्ति)

 

• However, as a constitutional/nominal head, the President acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister (Article 74), which exercises real, day-to-day executive power.

 

• This structure reflects India's parliamentary system, in which the President is the formal repository of executive authority while actual governance is carried out by the elected government.

 

• The President is also the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Similarly, Article 154 vests the executive power of a State in its Governor.

 

NOTE

 

• Council of Ministers headed by the PM (Option 1): Exercises real executive power in practice, but the Constitution formally vests that power in the President, on whose behalf the Council acts.

 

• Prime Minister (Option 2): Head of government and leader of the Council of Ministers, but not the constitutional repository of executive power.

 

• Chief Justice of the Supreme Court (Option 3): Heads the judiciary, an entirely separate organ of the State, not the executive.

question: Vempati Chinna Satyam was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1998. He was a _______ dancer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vempati Chinna Satyam (1929-2012) was a renowned exponent and reformer of the Kuchipudi classical dance form, credited with popularising it on the global stage and reshaping it into a distinct solo dance style beyond its dance-drama origins. (वेम्पति चिन्ना सत्यम — कुचिपुड़ी नृत्य)

 

• He founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Chennai (Madras) in 1963, which trained generations of Kuchipudi dancers and popularised the form worldwide.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Shri (1970) and the Padma Bhushan (1998) for his contribution to Indian classical dance.

 

• Kuchipudi originated in Andhra Pradesh, traditionally performed by Brahmin men in a village of the same name, and was originally a dance-drama form based on Hindu mythology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other noted Kuchipudi exponents include the dancer-duo Raja and Radha Reddy.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathak (Option 2): A North Indian classical dance form, associated with exponents such as Pandit Birju Maharaj.

 

• Manipuri (Option 3): A classical dance from Manipur, known for its gentle, graceful movements depicting Radha-Krishna themes.

 

• Kathakali (Option 4): A classical dance-drama of Kerala, known for elaborate costumes and expressive facial makeup.

question: ‘Do or die’ slogan is given by which of the following freedom fighter?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The “Do or Die” (Karo ya Maro) slogan was given by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942, at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, while launching the Quit India Movement. (करो या मरो — महात्मा गांधी)

 

• The slogan called upon every Indian to either win freedom or die trying, and marked one of the most decisive, mass-based phases of India's freedom struggle.

 

• The Quit India Movement (August Kranti) demanded an immediate end to British rule and was launched through a resolution passed at the All India Congress Committee's Bombay session.

 

• Following this speech, Gandhi and other senior Congress leaders were arrested; the movement nonetheless spread rapidly, becoming one of the largest civil disobedience movements of the freedom struggle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The resolution passed at this AICC session is popularly remembered as the Quit India Resolution.

 

NOTE

 

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Option 1): Known for the slogan “Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.”

 

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (Option 2): Known as the “Iron Man of India”, credited with the political integration of the princely states.

 

• Motilal Nehru (Option 4): A senior Congress leader and father of Jawaharlal Nehru, associated with the Nehru Report (1928), not this slogan.

question: In June 2022, NIPUN scheme was launched for skill training of _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is construction workers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In June 2022, the NIPUN (National Initiative for Promoting Upskilling of Nirman workers) scheme was launched by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), in association with industry bodies, to provide skill training and certification to construction workers. (निपुण योजना — निर्माण श्रमिकों का कौशल प्रशिक्षण)

 

• The scheme aims to train lakhs of construction-sector workers in core trades such as masonry, bar-bending, and plumbing, thereby improving productivity, safety, and employability across the construction industry.

 

• It is aligned with the government's broader Skill India Mission, seeking to formalise and upskill India's largely unorganised construction workforce.

 

• NIPUN partners with construction/real-estate companies and training providers to deliver both on-site and institutional training.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• This “NIPUN” scheme for construction workers is distinct from “NIPUN Bharat”, a separate Ministry of Education mission (launched July 2021) focused on foundational literacy and numeracy among school children.

 

NOTE

 

• Farmers (Option 1), medical practitioners (Option 2), government teachers (Option 3): None of these is the target group of the NIPUN (construction workers) scheme; each has its own separate skilling/training initiatives.

question: Which of the following folk dance forms is NOT associated with the state of Gujarat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hojagiri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hojagiri is a folk dance of the Reang (Bru) tribal community of Tripura, performed by young women balancing on earthen pitchers while balancing further objects on their heads, and is NOT associated with Gujarat. (होजागिरी नृत्य — त्रिपुरा)

 

• Dandiya Raas and Garba are traditional folk dances of Gujarat, performed extensively during Navratri — Dandiya uses wooden sticks in rhythmic patterns, while Garba is performed in circular formation, often around a lamp or image of the Goddess.

 

• Bhavai is a folk dance-drama form of Gujarat (and parts of Rajasthan), known for performers balancing multiple earthen or brass pitchers on their heads while dancing.

 

• Gujarat's rich folk-dance tradition (Garba, Dandiya, Bhavai) is central to its cultural identity, especially during festive seasons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tripura's tribal communities have several other regional folk dances performed at community festivals, alongside Hojagiri.

 

NOTE

 

• Dandiya (Option 2), Bhavai (Option 3), Garba (Option 4): All are genuine folk dance forms closely associated with the state of Gujarat.

question: Who was the first to accurately describe the rings of Saturn as a disc around the planet in 1655?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Christiaan Huygens.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens was the first to accurately describe Saturn's rings as a flat disc surrounding the planet without touching it, in 1655 (detailed in his later work *Systema Saturnium*, 1659). (क्रिस्टियान हाइगेंस — शनि के वलय)

 

• Earlier observers, including Galileo Galilei in 1610, had noticed unusual “appendages” or bulges around Saturn using less powerful telescopes, but could not correctly interpret them as a ring system.

 

• Huygens used an improved telescope of his own design to resolve these features clearly as a thin ring encircling Saturn.

 

• He also discovered Titan, Saturn's largest moon, in 1655.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Later, in 1675, Giovanni Cassini discovered a gap within Saturn's ring system, now known as the Cassini Division.

 

NOTE

 

• Hideki Yukawa (Option 1): A 20th-century Japanese physicist known for predicting the meson in particle physics, unrelated to this discovery.

 

• Galileo Galilei (Option 2): Observed unusual shapes around Saturn as early as 1610 but could not correctly identify them as a ring system.

 

• Giovanni Cassini (Option 4): Made later, more detailed observations of Saturn's rings — including discovering the Cassini Division — after Huygens's initial correct identification.

question: October and November months in India comes under which among the following seasons?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Autumn.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the seasonal classification followed in Indian climatology and geography textbooks, the months of October and November constitute the “Retreating/Post-Monsoon” or Autumn season, marking the withdrawal of the South-West Monsoon. (शरद ऋतु — अक्टूबर-नवंबर)

 

• During this season, monsoon winds retreat from North India towards the Bay of Bengal, bringing occasional rainfall to the south-eastern coast (Tamil Nadu) via the retreating/North-East monsoon.

 

• Temperatures begin to fall as skies clear, marking a transition period between the rainy season and the onset of winter.

 

• The commonly used four-fold seasonal classification of India is: Winter (December-February), Summer (March-May), Monsoon/Rainy (June-September), and Autumn/Retreating Monsoon (October-November).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The North-East (retreating) monsoon brings the bulk of annual rainfall to Tamil Nadu and parts of Andhra Pradesh during October-December.

 

NOTE

 

• Winter (Option 1): Occurs from December to February, marked by low temperatures across most of India.

 

• Summer (Option 2): Occurs from March to May, marked by rising temperatures ahead of the monsoon.

 

• Rainy (Option 3): The South-West Monsoon season, spanning June to September.

question: Which of the following countries hosted the first edition of the Summer Youth Olympic Games in 2010?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Singapore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Singapore hosted the first edition of the Summer Youth Olympic Games (YOG) in 2010, an event created by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) for athletes aged 14-18. (प्रथम ग्रीष्मकालीन यूथ ओलंपिक — सिंगापुर, 2010)

 

• The inaugural Games were held from 14-26 August 2010, with athletes from over 200 countries competing across a range of sporting disciplines.

 

• The Youth Olympic Games concept, proposed by then-IOC President Jacques Rogge, aims to promote Olympic values and encourage youth participation in sport, alongside cultural and educational programmes.

 

• The first Winter Youth Olympic Games followed at Innsbruck, Austria, in 2012.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The second Summer Youth Olympic Games were held in Nanjing, China (2014), followed by Buenos Aires, Argentina (2018).

 

NOTE

 

• China (Option 1): Hosted the second edition (Nanjing, 2014), not the first.

 

• Argentina (Option 3): Hosted the third edition (Buenos Aires, 2018), not the first.

 

• Senegal (Option 4): Slated to host a later edition (Dakar), not the first edition of 2010.

question: The height of stumps in cricket is ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 28 inches.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Laws of Cricket, the stumps must be 28 inches (71.1 cm) in height above the playing surface. (क्रिकेट की स्टंप्स की ऊंचाई — 28 इंच)

 

• Three stumps placed together, with two bails resting on top, form the wicket, which must have an overall width of 9 inches (22.86 cm).

 

• The bails, when correctly positioned, add a small additional height to the total wicket structure.

 

• Equipment dimensions in cricket, including the 22-yard (20.12 m) pitch length between the two sets of stumps, are standardised by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC), the custodian of the Laws of Cricket.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The cricket pitch measures 22 yards in length between the two sets of stumps at either end.

 

NOTE

 

• 20 inches (Option 2), 25 inches (Option 3), 22 inches (Option 4): None of these corresponds to the official stump height laid down in the Laws of Cricket; 28 inches is the correct standard.

question: Which of the following is a feature of Self-Help group?
option_1: The group takes care of the debt recovery.
option_2: There is a requirement of collateral.
option_3: These groups are classified as commercial banks.
option_4: The interest rates are generally high.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The group takes care of the debt recovery.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Self-Help Group (SHG) is a voluntary association of individuals, usually from similar socio-economic backgrounds (commonly rural women), who pool small savings and lend to members out of this common fund. (स्व-सहायता समूह — ऋण वसूली स्वयं समूह द्वारा)

 

• A key feature of SHGs is peer monitoring and group responsibility — the group itself takes responsibility for debt/loan recovery from its members, relying on social pressure and mutual trust rather than formal collateral or external recovery agents.

 

• SHGs typically function without requiring collateral security, since the group's collective guarantee substitutes for it, making credit accessible to the otherwise “unbankable” poor.

 

• SHGs are not classified as commercial banks; they are informal, member-based savings-and-credit groups, often linked to formal banks through the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (SBLP), pioneered by NABARD.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• SHGs generally charge moderate, member-decided interest rates, usually well below those charged by informal moneylenders, rather than uniformly “high” rates.

 

NOTE

 

• There is a requirement of collateral (Option 2): Incorrect — SHGs are known precisely for extending credit without demanding collateral.

 

• These groups are classified as commercial banks (Option 3): Incorrect — SHGs are informal groups, not licensed banking institutions.

 

• The interest rates are generally high (Option 4): Incorrect — offering more affordable credit than informal lenders is a defining strength of SHGs.

question: Rukmani Devi Arundale was a famous dancer of which Indian classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale (1904-1986) was a pioneering exponent and reformer of Bharatanatyam, credited with reviving and modernising this classical dance form and bringing it respectability on the public stage in the 20th century. (रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल — भरतनाट्यम)

 

• She founded Kalakshetra, an academy of dance and the arts in Chennai (then Madras), in 1936, which grew into a leading institution for training in Bharatanatyam and Carnatic music.

 

• She reworked the earlier Sadir/Devadasi style of dance into what is today known as Bharatanatyam, giving it a structured curriculum, refined aesthetics, and wider social acceptability.

 

• She was also a noted theosophist and animal welfare activist, and was nominated to the Rajya Sabha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• She was honoured with the Padma Bhushan and is remembered as one of the foremost cultural reformers of modern India.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathak (Option 2): A North Indian classical dance form, not associated with Rukmini Devi Arundale.

 

• Mohiniyattam (Option 3): A classical dance of Kerala, characterised by graceful, swaying movements.

 

• Kathakali (Option 4): A classical dance-drama of Kerala, known for elaborate costumes and facial expressions.
